exact_statement: For every finite probability P with nonempty mass a>0, supplied finite-CE subprobability R of mass s in(0,1] and positive tail mass w, let pi and M be their conditional nonempty laws. For any prescribed probability T on ALL nonempty labels and c in(0,1), among replacements preserving R vacuum, w and s and satisfying conditional x>=cT, the unique minimum complete CE replacement is x_j=max(cT_j,k*pi_j), with unique k>0 making sum x=1. Its minimum SIGNED price is a[D2(pi||x)-D2(pi||M)], including reference-only floors. At an actual frontier with original capacity B, all earlier bills U and full current terminal CE C, it is paid iff sum reached signed prices<=B-U-C, retaining every sibling and applying a disjoint sector weight once. This is a supplied-source theorem. On Boolean AND2 with full uniform spectrum and incoming R=(1/4,3/16,15/32,3/32), the SAME conditional floor x1>=1/2 has flexible minimum full price (1/4)log2(5/8)<0, but fixing incoming ratio5:1 on the other atoms gives minimum (1/4)log2(9/8)>0. Universal influence-priced initial sources and useful mandatory policy compatibility remain open.
